deviations_from_card: (1) Commit order is feat, then test, then package.json, then docs. Cases 1-6 were red until ledger.cjs existed, so the test commit follows the fix. Case 7 (guard) was green throughout. (2) Case 4's CLI half checks parseArgs() in process: no --recertify is spawned, because that would start codex. parseArgs rules: a word after --recertify that is neither a flag nor a Character id is a run, so '--recertify <run>' parses as before. Nothing, a flag or a Character id after it means the ledger. (3) Case 6's CLI check spawns `linga-text.cjs --status --runs <temp copy>` with an empty PATH, so no codex could start. The in-process statusCommand() is checked with the codexText call count unchanged. (4) New option `--runs <dir>`, which replaces uat/runs/ for every mode. The tests need it so they can point --status at a temp copy. (5) finishLedger does not write a recertify.md. It stamps the originating findings.json files and rewrites OPEN.md, which is the card's flow. renderRecertify stays per-run. (6) instrumentOf() now also hashes ledger.cjs. (7) README.md's layout now also lists verdict.cjs, which wave 1 left out. Nothing else differs.
notes: The committed runs are never rewritten. Global ids ('<runId>/<id>', a rerun's runId being '<run>/recert-<k>') are derived on every ledger() read. A ledger recertify writes the following. (a) The rerun's run.json gains `ledger.prior` = {character: {journey: [{id: <global id>, run, type, dimension, title, expected, got, evidence, recurrence}]}}, exactly what each judge is shown. The child reads it (env UAT_LEDGER=1). (b) The judge answers prior[] by global id. (c) In the rerun's own findings.json, a restated gap carries `recurs: '<run>/<id>'` (a global id). A per-run rerun writes a local id there, and ledger.cjs resolves both (a ref with no '/' is read in the run the rerun sits in). (d) finishLedger stamps every open row of each answered gap, in the findings.json of the run that owns it, under the row's own local id. It writes only the existing fields: recertify_run = '<home>/recert-<k>', recertify_status, recertify_evidence, resolution 'fixed' for not-seen, and recurrence+1 and recurred_as (the rerun's local id) for recurs. (e) It writes <runs>/OPEN.md. A gap is a recurs-chain named by its newest row and open while that row is open. unasked counts the later runs that ran the pair without the gap in a record's prior[] or a recertify_run stamp. On the committed runs: 186 open in 36 pairs across 5 runs, 108 open gaps unasked by a later run, recurrence 1 everywhere, drained 0 of 5. Verdicts are not part of the ledger, so the ledger reads no verdict (stored or code). The rerun lives under the top-level run holding the newest planned gap (today 2026-09-15-lt-recert2-goal, as recert-1). The 14 hand-stamped fixed rows in 2026-09-15-lt (recertify_run '2026-09-15-lt-recert') count as asked in that run. No live model call was made anywhere: the tests use the stub judge and my manual check was --status on a temp copy with an empty PATH. No OPEN.md was written into uat/runs.
